brief: Our own roof is the biggest object in the picture and, below the ridge, nothing is on it. Shoot it yourself before you start — at 1600x950 and at 390x844 the near block is 14-20% of the frame and reads as one flat blue-grey field. The cause is bounded and known: roofBirdSpot() and the cat are capped at ROOF_DMAX 82.2 (band ROOF_N 81.8..ROOF_S 84.6), which is the band visible at EVERY framing, because at a short 1200x720 sillTop() cuts the surface at row ~84.9. Everything south of that is inert slate at the two framings where the roof is largest. Give the lower roof something to be. It is a working roof seen from an upstairs window: the leads and valley gutters between the party walls, a flat behind the parapet, a water tank, a pigeon loft, washing pegged out on a fine day, a cat's route across the whole slope rather than along one line. Take the swing — a 150-300 line diff is expected and welcome. This is a 4b: it must change the shape of the map, so it must move a census scalar. passages, tileKinds and speciesKinds have not moved in 109 iterations and structures has moved once; move one of them, re-pin with `census.mjs --save-baseline`, and SAY SO in the ledger entry.
successLooksLike: On a phone and at 1600x950 the bottom fifth of the picture is somewhere with things happening on it, and a thirty-second look finds at least one of them without being told where. A census scalar has moved and the baseline is re-pinned.
avoid: Do not widen the general birds[] roll to reach the roof — the roof has its own source and its own cap, and widening the shared one makes the lawn and the roof compete (#92, #106). Do not bound anything new in ROWS: around a light well the same row is 1.7 of depth lower on a lip than on the pitch. If you extend the life band south you must clip it with nearHidden(); the blink as something crosses the sill line at 1200x720 is an accepted cost of this brief, but measure it and say how big it is.
